issues.quote: Madame plays Chopin when she is troubled. Everyone in this house knows that.
issues.fact: R2 says only that "Madame's piano" began and stopped. It does not say who was playing or that Madame was at the piano.
issues.misreading: A solver could conclude that Madame was at the piano from 10:58 to 11:11 by the kitchen clock, which places her whereabouts during the window. The sheet gives no such placement.

issues.quote: I did not see her go up the stairs, and I did not hear her cry.
issues.fact: The sheet says nothing about Madame going up the stairs or about any crying, so this has no basis in the facts.
issues.misreading: The denial could be read as a hint that Madame did go up the stairs, which would place her near the atelier. That is a whereabouts claim the sheet does not support.

issues.fact: R1 names the woman as "Fräulein Lina" and never gives the surname Ruedi. The transcript never links the two names.
issues.misreading: A careful solver could take Ruedi and Lina to be two different people, so the 10:47 kitchen visit might be attributed to the wrong woman.

issues.quote: nobody in this house was ever late for anything until tonight
issues.fact: The sheet gives no sense that anyone was late tonight or that lateness is a factor in the events.
issues.misreading: The line hints that something happened tonight that made someone late, which could suggest a timing or duration point the sheet does not make.

issues.quote: I was not thinking about the bench or the watches.
issues.fact: The sheet mentions no watches in the atelier and does not describe any watches or their readings.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the mention of watches as a hint that watches of interest were in the atelier, adding an unsupported clock-related detail.
